one_line: A multi-vendor marketplace where buyer and seller agents negotiate a complete deal before human confirmation.
what_it_does: Searches products, manages carts and coupons, and conducts multi-round negotiation over price, quantity, add-ons, shipping, and coupons, with a human confirmation gate.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared negotiation state and explicit economic transition rules make multi-dimensional bargaining substantially more reliable than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes buyer and seller agents negotiating over several rounds.
ABOUT states every state change goes through OffersService.applyTurn and enforces budget/floor limits.
ABOUT states purchase cannot occur until human confirmation.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent full storefront and negotiation flow, with a live demo link and multiple gallery/frame surfaces, though no readable end-to-end success state is strongly established.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
ABOUT specifies Next.js frontend, Spring backend, database migrations, and a single mutation path.
Frame-sheet evidence shows repeated dark storefront/application states, but small text limits verification.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real shopping desire—delegating tedious bargaining while preserving buyer control—and extends negotiation beyond a single price.
impact_evidence: PITCH identifies complete deal negotiation across price, quantity, add-ons, shipping, and coupons.
ABOUT identifies a multi-vendor storefront with 95k+ products and human confirmation.

ABOUT frames the novel unit of negotiation as a multi-dimensional deal rather than price alone.
usability_note: Human confirmation and visible deal terms support trust; the multi-round flow may be complex.
standouts: Explicit economic invariants and shared state
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP delta and distinctive commerce workflow with credible implementation evidence.

leverage_rationale: Typed tools expose the live architecture graph and analysis engine directly, enabling operations that screenshot-based agents cannot perform comparably.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT explicitly says screenshot agents cannot read or analyze the canvas graph.
PITCH and ABOUT describe shared graph editing, simulate-failure, cost estimation, linting, and Terraform generation.
ABOUT reports a /learn route with 13 live WebMCP tool schemas.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a highly coherent architecture workflow with visible graph states and concrete failure, resilience, cost, and code outputs; some end-to-end details remain claimed rather than directly observed.

Frame sheet shows progression from sparse to populated dark canvas/node-graph states with denser analysis panels.
ABOUT gives concrete outputs including resilience 61/100 and before/after monthly pricing.
impact_rationale: Solutions architects and infrastructure teams have a concrete, consequential need to reason about resilience/cost trade-offs and generate deployable configuration.
impact_evidence: PITCH targets cloud architecture design and failure analysis.
ABOUT describes blast-radius analysis, DDIA-cited findings, provider swaps, cost deltas, and Terraform generation.
creativity_rationale: The shared architecture canvas plus live failure simulation and agent collaboration is an ambitious, memorable interaction model tailored to WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human edit the same topology model.
PITCH combines design, failure propagation, pricing, linting, and code generation in one collaborative surface.
usability_note: A shared visual model and explain-per-resource actions appear well matched to the target workflow.
standouts: WebMCP is plausibly indispensable for graph/state operations
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, credible execution, and strong practical impact for infrastructure design.

one_line: A correctness-gated WebGPU experiment lab that exposes safe verification and profiling to browser agents.
what_it_does: Runs local CPU/GPU proof-of-work-style experiments, compares results, reports provenance and performance, and refuses unsupported conclusions.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools can run gated experiments and share exact result state more safely than generic UI automation, though the underlying lab is usable without an agent.
leverage_evidence: PITCH states agents run correctness-gated experiments and share state with the human UI.
ABOUT describes four WebMCP tools, CPU reference verification, test vectors, profiling, and workgroup experiments.
ABOUT explicitly describes refusal of unsupported performance conclusions.
execution_rationale: The project appears substantial and safety-conscious, but the frame evidence is largely static UI and the visible packaging screenshot shows a zero-result CPU state rather than a completed GPU experiment.
execution_evidence: Demo is alive and repository is public.
Frame sheet shows a dark verification dashboard with CPU/GPU fields and status cards.
Screenshot visibly reports CPU JavaScript mode, GPU hashing inactive, zero hashes, and unimplemented compute shader.
impact_rationale: It offers a credible niche value for developers and researchers who need browser-local GPU correctness and performance verification without unsafe mining claims.
impact_evidence: ABOUT defines a local research and verification tool with no blockchain, wallet, pool, or payout integration.
PITCH identifies correctness gating and safety boundaries as core behavior.
creativity_rationale: Combining WebGPU experimentation with agent safety gates, provenance, and refusal behavior is a thoughtful and distinctive direction.
creativity_evidence: PITCH emphasizes refusing unsupported performance conclusions.
ABOUT describes CapStash Core-derived vectors, CPU reference checks, and guided/advanced modes.
usability_note: The dashboard is structured, but the visible zero-result state and technical complexity limit confidence in a polished user path.
red_flags: ABOUT explicitly says the project had already grown into a fairly complete human-operated lab before the challenge.
Visible screenshot shows no active GPU implementation and zero measurements.
advance_reason: Distinctive safety and verification angle with meaningful agent leverage, despite incomplete visible GPU evidence.

one_line: A meeting scheduler where human and agent participants vote, counter-propose, and converge on a time.

usability_note: Human organizer approval and visible logs provide a strong trust model for multi-party scheduling.
standouts: Visible action attribution and approval gate
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP fit and clear audience value with a distinctive negotiation model.

advance_reason: Outstanding evidence-backed execution, transformative WebMCP leverage, and unusually original creative interaction.
